_comment: The dependency set as data, because it is written in four places and nothing compared them.
conandata.yml is what Conan resolves; metadata.json:dependencies is what the template's CMake
reads, in four buckets; baremetal_white_list says which ones may appear on a bare-metal target;
and NOTICE says what we redistribute. `deps_gate.py` makes the four agree.
`used_from` is not prose: the gate opens that file and looks for that string, so 'this dependency
is used' is a measurement rather than a claim. An entry with no consumer must say `why_unused`
instead, which is how a deliberately kept dependency (gaps G-4) stays visible.
`license` is the SPDX id we rely on, `license_evidence` says where that was read from -- the
package's own recipe or licence file on the machine, or an explicit marker that it could not be
checked here. A `license_status` of `unverified` is only allowed for something we do not
redistribute (D3): an unverified licence is acceptable in a build-only dependency and not in
something we hand to someone else.
`redistributed` drives D4: our Conan package does not embed its dependencies, so this is false
for all six today and NOTICE names none of them -- correctly. The rule exists so that vendoring
a dependency into the tree cannot happen without an attribution line appearing.

Attribution is a field, not a file (2026-11-26, owner challenge): D4 used to read a notice file, which forced a new root-level document to exist for a hypothetical -- nothing here is redistributed today, so its marked section was empty. `attribution` sits next to the licence it belongs to; when a component is actually vendored, that text is what a generated notice file would carry.

entries.license_evidence: conan recipe license = "Zlib"; package ships s/src/LICENSE (Jean-loup Gailly / Mark Adler notice)
entries.why: the template's C demo unit (src/ctest.c) compresses a buffer with it; kept from the template, not yet used by the kernel layer

entries.license_evidence: conan recipe license = "BSD-3-Clause"; package ships s/src/COPYING
entries.why: the template's C demo unit (src/ctest.c) matches a regular expression with it; kept from the template

entries.license_evidence: package ships p/licenses/COPYING.MPL2 among LGPL/GPL/BSD/Apache alternatives; MPL-2.0 is the one we rely on
entries.why: the template's C++ demo unit (src/cpptest.cpp) solves a small system with it; kept from the template

entries.license_evidence: conan recipe license = "MIT" (this machine's cache); the recipe also installs its LICENSE into licenses/
entries.why: the only dependency allowed on a bare-metal target (metadata.baremetal_white_list); used by src/etl.cpp

entries.license_evidence: conan recipe license = "BSD-3-Clause"; package ships s/src/LICENSE (Google Inc. notice)
entries.why: the test framework; infra bucket, never part of the shipped library

entries.license_evidence: not verifiable on this machine: pybind11 is not in the Conan cache because the bindings are disabled (gaps G-31); the id is the upstream one and this entry must be re-checked the moment the bindings are enabled
entries.why: the Python bindings demo (api/python_bindings.cpp); metadata.enable_python_bindings stays false, so this is a build-only dependency

entries.license_evidence: upstream repository ships LICENSE (Apache-2.0); the local recipe packages it into licenses/LICENSE
entries.why: the optional vendor backend for Cortex-M: it is resolved only when the with_cmsis_nn option is on, and its kernels are meant for exactly the bare-metal targets this library supports
